SERP & Algorithm Signals.what_happened: Google's John Mueller: Eventually Systems Will Catch The AI Spam & Tricks. Google's John Mueller was interviewed by…

sources.name: Search Engine Roundtable
sources.excerpt: Google's John Mueller: Eventually Systems Will Catch The AI Spam & Tricks. Google's John Mueller was interviewed by David Iwanow, where he shared information on AI-generated content, the future of SEO, technical SEO, the crawl stats report, redirect chains, ecommerce product data and much more. John was asked about tactics, such as listicles, being used to rank well in AI Search, and he said that eventually the systems will catch up, so don't use those cheap, easy, and fast tactics.
sources.author: Search Engine Roundtable

AI Search / GEO.what_happened: I find it interesting how much of Google's messaging over the past two years has revolved around its "search query…

sources.name: lilyraynyc
sources.excerpt: I find it interesting how much of Google's messaging over the past two years has revolved around its "search query growth rate." (You know, like how every follow-up message in AI Mode can count as another search query 🙄) But where are the metrics showing that search is actually getting better? Where's the evidence that AI-generated answers are more accurate and trustworthy than what was there before? How do we know users are genuinely having a better search experience now with AI, beyond vague claims that "users really like it"? Do more search queries inherently mean users are having a better experience? What if they're searching more because AI Overviews or AI Mode didn't give them what…
sources.author: @lilyraynyc
